entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
Cherenkov radiation is a phenomenon of electromagnetic radiation emitted when a charged particle passes through a dielectric medium at a speed greater than the phase velocity of light in that medium. 

This process was first observed by Soviet physicist Pavel Cherenkov in 1934, and it has since been recognized as a fundamental aspect of particle physics. 

The discovery of Cherenkov radiation led to a deeper understanding of the behavior of charged particles in matter, and it has been used in a variety of applications, including the detection of high-energy particles and the study of nuclear reactions. 

One of the most notable consequences of Cherenkov radiation is the blue glow that it produces, which has been used to create striking visual effects in art and entertainment.

As physicist Dr. Brian Cox notes, 'Cherenkov radiation is a beautiful example of how the laws of physics can be used to create something truly breathtaking.'
